_comment: Hand-read values for the line chart photos in sample-images/, used to measure how
accurate the extraction is (tests/test_line_graph.py and tests/check_accuracy.py).
Each chart was straightened with chartx.main.preprocess, then value gridlines were drawn
over it every quarter of an axis step and the marker on each data point was read off by eye.
The charts are hand-drawn, so these are what was actually drawn, not round numbers the
artist may have meant: Mar on the coffee chart sits a shade above 150, and Jun a shade
'lines' is keyed by pen colour, because the charts have no legend saying which series is
which. 'photo' names a file in sample-images/.
'tolerance' is a fraction of the y-axis range (max - min). The extraction currently comes
in at 1.1% on average and 2.3% at worst, so 6% leaves room for the OCR reading the axis
labels slightly differently between builds, without letting a real regression through.
Run tests/check_accuracy.py to see where it actually stands.
